question: Does aggressive finalist-heavy root Sequential Halving at an exact 1000 simulations per root confirm its exploratory online advantage over ordinary UCT c=25?

hypotheses.null: The historical 43/64 versus 32/64 result was sampling noise or configuration-specific and will not produce a positive paired confirmation.
hypotheses.treatment: Aggressive early screening plus finalist-heavy allocation improves fixed-budget online decisions enough to increase paired wins without material floor harm.

population.freshness: No exact 933999 or 934000-934127 experiment block was found in maintained experiment evidence before preregistration.

primary_metric: paired win-rate difference treatment minus control
integrity_gate: Both arms exit zero and contain exactly the same 128 unique seeds.
No conversion, semantic-resolution, transaction, knowledge, or bestbench seed failure occurs.
Every Silver simulation total is divisible by 1000.
Every Silver telemetry record is structurally parseable.
The canary passes these checks before either cohort arm starts.

confirmed_promising: paired win improvement is at least 5 percentage points
paired 95% win-difference lower bound is above zero
paired mean-floor 95% lower bound is at least -1.0
decision_rule.inconclusive: The win interval includes zero or the floor non-harm bound fails, despite operational validity.
decision_rule.rejected: The treatment is directionally nonpositive on wins or has a severe operational failure.
decision_rule.runtime: Descriptive, not an exclusion at the historical approximately 1.107x ratio; flag as severe operational regression only above 1.25x control.

non_goals: No combination of root c with Sequential Halving.
No additional hyperparameter selection from this block.
No default change or promotion before interpreting the frozen gate.
